patients.summary: Two-time cancer survivor (triple-negative right breast cancer 2018, cervical SCC 2021) with right-arm lymphedema who develops radiation proctitis, then metastatic midgut NET with carcinoid syndrome on lanreotide, then a lymphedema/radiation-associated angiosarcoma of the right chest wall treated with resection and paclitaxel.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 61F, establishing after her longtime PCP retired.

She has been through a lot in a short stretch. In 2018 she was treated for a right breast cancer (invasive ductal, triple-negative, stage IIA): lumpectomy with sentinel node and then a full axillary dissection, chemotherapy through a port on the right, and breast radiation finished in the fall of 2018. Port came out in 2019. The right arm has been swollen ever since the node dissection; she wears a compression sleeve most days and a gauntlet when gardening. Grade 2 per her therapist.

Then early this year she was diagnosed with cervical squamous cell carcinoma, stage IB2. Radical hysterectomy with both tubes and ovaries in the spring, pelvic radiation after, wrapped up in July. Gyn onc is following her every 6 months. She is tired but says the worst is behind her.

Told at the old office that her bones were thin (DXA last year). No fractures.

Meds: none. Not on any supplements. NKDA.
FH: mother had breast cancer after menopause, in her 70s (74). Father MI at 68. One sister, well.
SH: taught second and third grade for many years, on disability since the breast cancer treatment. Never smoked. Does not drink. Lives in Belchertown.

ROS: fatigue, otherwise negative. No bowel or bladder change, no bleeding since surgery, no bone pain, no cough.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Right breast with healed lumpectomy scar and post-radiation skin change, no masses; left breast normal. No axillary or supraclavicular nodes. Right arm visibly fuller than the left, non-pitting, skin intact. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed midline scar. No leg edema.

Assessment/plan
1. Breast cancer survivor, 3 years out. Survivorship with outside breast oncology; yearly diagnostic mammograms.
2. Cervical cancer, recently completed treatment. Surveillance with gyn onc.
3. RUE lymphedema, chronic. Continue sleeve. Will refer to lymphedema therapy for refitting when she is ready.
4. Osteopenia. Get prior DXA report. Repeat at a 2-3 year interval.
5. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. Hep C and HIV screening once, she agreed. Flu and COVID booster at a nurse visit next month. Records requested.

RTC for wellness visit in the spring.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Heather, your blood work from Monday is all normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid, and cholesterol. The hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to do. See you in the spring, and the nurse will see you for the vaccines in October.

documents.title: Prior primary care and cancer center records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office and the outside cancer center (138 pages), scanned to media.

Summary for the chart:
- Prior PCP: screening colonoscopy 2017, normal to the cecum, no polyps, 10-year interval. DXA 05/2020: lowest T-score -1.7 at the left femoral neck, osteopenia. Routine labs normal through 2020.
- Breast oncology: right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR/HER2 negative, stage IIA, 02/2018. Lumpectomy with sentinel node biopsy then completion axillary dissection 03/2018. Adjuvant chemotherapy via right subclavian port 2018. Whole-breast radiation completed 10/2018. Port removed 03/2019. Survivorship visits yearly.
- Gyn oncology: cervical squamous cell carcinoma stage IB2, 02/2021. Radical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 04/2021. Pelvic external beam radiation completed 07/2021. Surveillance every 6 months.
- Allergies on all records: NKDA.

documents.body: Here for flu vaccine and COVID booster. Screening questions negative, no fever today. Flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Pfizer booster IM left deltoid (right arm avoided, lymphedema). Waited 15 minutes, tolerated well. VIS given.

documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - SURVEILLANCE VISIT
Date of service: 01/06/2022
Diagnosis: cervical squamous cell carcinoma, FIGO IB2, s/p radical hysterectomy, BSO and adjuvant pelvic radiation (completed 07/2021).

Interval: 6 months from completion of therapy. Mild fatigue. No vaginal bleeding or discharge, no pelvic pain, no leg swelling. Bowel and bladder function at baseline.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.
Exam: no inguinal or supraclavicular adenopathy. Speculum: vaginal cuff intact, healed, mild post-radiation pallor, no lesions. Bimanual/rectovaginal: no masses or nodularity.
Vaginal cuff cytology obtained: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
Impression: no evidence of disease.
Plan: return in 6 months with pelvic MRI before the visit. Vaginal dilator use reviewed.

reports.text: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis. History of right breast cancer treated with lumpectomy and radiation 2018. Comparison 02/2021. Breasts are scattered fibroglandular density. Right breast post-lumpectomy architectural distortion and skin thickening at the surgical site, stable. No suspicious mass, calcifications or new distortion in either breast.
reports.conclusion: Benign post-treatment change, right breast. BI-RADS 2. Annual diagnostic mammogram.

documents.title: Diagnostic mammogram result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Diagnostic mammogram report received from the outside breast imaging center, BI-RADS 2. Routed to PCP. Patient will see it in the portal.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV. Heather is 61, on Medicare through disability.

Since fall: saw gyn onc in January, cuff cytology negative, no evidence of disease. Mammogram last month BI-RADS 2. Energy slowly coming back; walking 30 min most days with her sister. Sleeve is wearing out and the fit is poor since she lost some weight during treatment.

Functional: independent, drives, manages finances. No falls. Hearing and vision fine (glasses). Lives alone, sister nearby. Advance directive: has a health care proxy (sister), copy requested.
PHQ-9 3.
Meds none. NKDA.

Exam: vitals charted. Comfortable. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Breasts: right lumpectomy scar, radiation change, no mass; left normal. Axillae clear. Abdomen soft. RUE non-pitting swelling, unchanged. Legs without edema.

Plan
- Shingrix #1 today, #2 in two months.
- Lymphedema therapy referral for measurement and a new sleeve.
- CBC, CMP, vitamin D.
- Colonoscopy due 2027. Mammogram yearly. Cervical surveillance per gyn onc.
- DXA next spring.

documents.title: Breast Oncology survivorship visit
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
BREAST MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - SURVIVORSHIP
Visit date: 03/24/2022
61-year-old woman with right breast IDC, triple-negative, stage IIA, diagnosed 02/2018, treated with lumpectomy, SLNB and completion ALND, adjuvant chemotherapy and whole-breast radiation (completed 10/2018). Also treated in 2021 for cervical SCC, now under gyn onc surveillance.

She feels well apart from fatigue. No new breast changes, bone pain, cough, headache or weight loss.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.
Exam: well. Right breast post-surgical and radiation change without mass. Left breast normal. No regional adenopathy. Right arm lymphedema, stable.
Mammogram 02/08/2022: BI-RADS 2.

Assessment: no evidence of recurrence, 4 years from diagnosis.
Plan: continue annual diagnostic mammography. Return in 1 year; after the 5-year mark we will transition survivorship to her PCP.

documents.title: Lymphedema therapy evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT REHABILITATION - LYMPHEDEMA EVALUATION
Date: 04/14/2022
Referral: chronic secondary lymphedema RUE after ALND (2018).
Subjective: arm heavy by evening, sleeve loose. No cellulitis episodes. Right-hand dominant.
Objective: skin intact, Stemmer sign positive at the right second digit, circumferential measurements taken and recorded in the therapy flowsheet. No pitting.
Assessment: stable grade 2 lymphedema, poorly fitted garment.
Plan: measured for custom flat-knit sleeve and gauntlet (2 sets), home program of self manual lymph drainage and exercises reviewed, 4 visits. Garment Rx request sent to PCP.

documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - SURVEILLANCE
Date of service: 07/07/2022
Cervical SCC IB2, one year from completion of adjuvant pelvic radiation.

MRI pelvis with and without contrast (06/30/2022): post-hysterectomy and post-oophorectomy pelvis. Vaginal cuff smooth without mass or abnormal enhancement. Low T2 signal fibrotic change in the parametrial and presacral soft tissues consistent with post-radiation fibrosis. No pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Bladder and rectum unremarkable.

She notes occasional pelvic tightness, no bleeding, no pain. Bowel and bladder at baseline.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.
Exam: cuff intact with radiation pallor; firm, smooth parametrial tissues on rectovaginal exam, no nodularity. Cytology: negative.
Impression: no evidence of recurrence. Post-radiation pelvic fibrosis.
Plan: continue dilator use, pelvic floor PT offered and declined for now. Visits every 6 months through year 2, then yearly.

documents.body:
Six-month check.
Lymphedema: new custom sleeves since June, much more comfortable, finished therapy and does the drainage routine at night. No infections.
Gyn onc July: MRI showed scar-type change in the pelvis from radiation, no cancer. She gets an occasional pulling feeling low in the pelvis, not painful.
Feels like herself again; volunteering at the library reading program twice a week.

- Lymphedema RUE, stable on new garments.
- Post-radiation pelvic fibrosis, noted from gyn onc; symptoms mild.
- CBC today since she asked about fatigue earlier in the year.
- Flu and new bivalent COVID at a nurse visit in October.

Subsequent AWV.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Lumbar spine L1-L4 BMD T-score -1.3. Left femoral neck T-score -1.9. Left total hip T-score -1.5. Right hip not scanned per protocol. FRAX 10-year probability: major osteoporotic fracture 12%, hip fracture 1.6%. Comparison 05/2020 outside study: left femoral neck T-score -1.7.

documents.title: Bone density result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Heather - your bone density shows osteopenia, a little lower at the hip than in 2020 (-1.9 vs -1.7). Your 10-year fracture risk score is under the level where we would start a bone medicine. Keep the walking and weights going and aim for calcium-rich foods. We will recheck in a couple of years. Your blood work from the 7th was normal too.

orders.reason: rectal bleeding, incomplete evacuation, weight loss after pelvic radiation

documents.title: Office Visit - Rectal bleeding
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: blood with bowel movements.

She has noticed bright red blood on the tissue and sometimes in the bowl, off and on for about six months. Thought it was hemorrhoids and waited. Also a sense that she never quite finishes, going back two or three times. No black stools, no belly pain. Weight down about 3.5 kg since spring without trying (68 -> 64.5). Appetite okay. Pelvic radiation finished July 2021. Colonoscopy 2017 was normal.

NKDA, no meds.

Exam: vitals charted. Thin, comfortable. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. External exam without hemorrhoids or fissure; she preferred to defer the digital exam to GI, who will scope her.

A/P: rectal bleeding with tenesmus-type symptoms and weight loss in a woman with prior pelvic radiation. Radiation proctitis is the leading thought but this needs a colonoscopy. Urgent GI referral placed; they will do labs and scope. Call if bleeding gets heavier, dizziness, or black stools.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION AND COLONOSCOPY
Date: 10/02/2023
Referring: primary care

Reason: rectal bleeding.

HPI: 63-year-old woman with intermittent bright red rectal bleeding for roughly half a year and a persistent feeling of incomplete emptying. Denies abdominal pain. Weight has dropped 5 kg over the past four months. History of cervical SCC treated in 2021 with radical hysterectomy/BSO and pelvic external beam radiation; right breast cancer 2018 treated with surgery, chemotherapy and radiation. Prior colonoscopy 2017 normal.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: negative for colorectal cancer.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol. Retired teacher.

Exam: vitals normal. Abdomen benign. Digital rectal exam: no palpable mass; bright red blood on the glove.

Labs today: Hgb 10.2 g/dL, MCV 85 fL, WBC 6.0, platelets 250.

Colonoscopy (same day, MAC sedation): prep good. Cecum reached, appendiceal orifice photographed. Colon from cecum to sigmoid normal, no polyps. Rectum: pale mucosa, friable to scope contact, with numerous telangiectasias limited to the rectum. No ulceration, stricture or mass. Retroflexion confirms changes extend to the dentate line.

Impression:
1. Chronic radiation proctitis, causing hematochezia.
2. Normocytic anemia, likely from chronic blood loss.

Plan: argon plasma coagulation of the rectal telangiectasias, likely two sessions about 8 weeks apart; first scheduled 11/06. Avoid straining; fiber as tolerated. CBC through primary care in a few months.

documents.title: Question about the GI procedure
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The GI doctor wants to do something called argon plasma for the bleeding. Is that safe with all the radiation I had down there? I trust you, just want your opinion before I go ahead.

documents.title: RE: Question about the GI procedure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Argon plasma coagulation is the usual treatment for the kind of bleeding blood vessels radiation leaves in the rectum. It is done through the scope, seals the vessels with heat, and most people need one to three sessions. It is a sensible next step given your blood count is down. Go ahead and keep the November date, and we will check your counts after.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu and 2023-24 COVID given IM, left deltoid both (no injections right arm). Tolerated. Reminded her to bring the GI procedure paperwork to her next visit.

documents.title: Flexible sigmoidoscopy with argon plasma coagulation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPY REPORT
Procedure: flexible sigmoidoscopy with argon plasma coagulation
Date: 11/06/2023
Indication: hematochezia from chronic radiation proctitis; anemia.
Sedation: MAC. Allergies: NKDA.
Findings: friable rectal mucosa with multiple telangiectasias, distal 10 cm. Sigmoid normal to 35 cm.
Intervention: APC to the larger telangiectatic areas, low flow, short pulses. Not all lesions treated, staged approach planned.
Complications: none.
Plan: second session in about 8 weeks. Expect some spotting for a few days.

documents.title: Flexible sigmoidoscopy with APC, session 2
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPY REPORT
Procedure: flexible sigmoidoscopy with argon plasma coagulation, second session
Date: 01/08/2024
Since November she reports bleeding only occasionally and lightly.
Findings: treated areas healing with pale scar. Residual telangiectasias in the distal rectum.
Intervention: APC to residual lesions.
Complications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Impression: chronic radiation proctitis, improved after APC.
Plan: no scheduled session; return if bleeding recurs. CBC with PCP.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology annual surveillance
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - ANNUAL SURVEILLANCE
Visit 01/04/2024. Cervical SCC IB2 (2021), 2.5 years from therapy.
New since last visit: radiation proctitis diagnosed by GI in October, treated with APC.
Allergies: NKDA. Meds: none.
Exam: no adenopathy. Cuff atrophic, intact. Rectovaginal exam with stable fibrotic change.
Cuff cytology: negative.
Impression: no evidence of disease. Yearly visits from here.

reports.text: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 2023 and 2022. Stable right lumpectomy site distortion and skin thickening. No suspicious findings in either breast.

documents.title: CBC after APC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 10.7, up a little from 10.2 in October. Bleeding now occasional per GI's January note. Recheck at next visit. Portal message sent.

orders.order: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast

documents.title: Office Visit - Fatigue and flushing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
She comes in because "something is off." Over the winter, increasing tiredness, and spells where her face goes hot and red for a few minutes, several times a week, sometimes after eating. Loose watery stools a few times a day for a couple of months, no blood (rectal bleeding much better after the APC). Some wheezing at night that she never had before. Ankles puffy by evening. Weight keeps drifting down, 61.5 kg today.
No fever, no travel, no antibiotics, nobody sick at home.
No meds. NKDA. Never smoker.

Exam: vitals charted. Thin. Face not flushed at present. Lungs clear today, no wheeze. Heart regular, no murmur heard. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge not felt. Trace ankle edema both sides. RUE lymphedema, baseline.

Assessment: weight loss with flushing, diarrhea and wheeze. The bowel symptoms are not what radiation proctitis does. Needs imaging of the abdomen. With the ankle swelling and fatigue I want cardiology to look at her heart.
Plan: CMP and TSH today. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast. Cardiology referral. Stool diary. Will call with CT result.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: unintentional weight loss, diarrhea. Technique: multiphase CT with IV contrast. Liver: several hypervascular lesions enhancing avidly on the arterial phase with washout, the largest 2.4 cm (measured in axial plane). Spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys normal. No biliary dilatation. Bowel without obstruction. No ascites or adenopathy. Pelvis: post-hysterectomy and oophorectomy, post-radiation soft-tissue stranding in the presacral space and parametria. Bones without destructive lesion.
reports.conclusion: Several hypervascular liver lesions, indeterminate; a hypervascular metastatic process such as neuroendocrine tumor should be considered. Post-treatment pelvic change.

documents.title: CT result discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Heather with CT. Several spots in the liver that light up with contrast. Explained these need a diagnosis and that the pattern can go with a slow-growing hormone-making tumor, which would fit the flushing and diarrhea, but we need tests to say. She was quiet, then asked good questions; sister with her on speaker. Cardiology is 4/15 and I sent them the CT. I will also message the cardiologist. She knows to call me any time.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date: 04/15/2024
Referred by primary care for fatigue and ankle swelling.

HPI: 63-year-old woman, treated for right breast cancer (2018) and cervical cancer (2021, pelvic radiation), with chronic right arm lymphedema and post-radiation pelvic fibrosis, seen by GI six months ago for chronic radiation proctitis. Over several months she has grown more fatigued, has frequent facial flushing episodes and has lost weight unintentionally. Several watery stools a day, no blood or mucus, unchanged by dietary changes. No travel, antibiotics or sick contacts. New intermittent wheeze, mostly at night; no asthma history and she has never smoked. Appetite fair. Ankles swell by evening.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother breast cancer at 74; father MI at 68; sister healthy. No family history of colorectal cancer, neuroendocrine tumors or sarcoma.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol; retired elementary school teacher on disability.

Exam: vital signs normal. Comfortable appearing. Subtle darkening of the skin around both eyes. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Mild bilateral lower extremity edema. Right arm lymphedema.

Data: Hgb 11.1 g/dL, normocytic. ECG: sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no ST changes. CT abdomen/pelvis 04/03/2024: several hypervascular liver lesions.

Assessment: flushing, secretory-type diarrhea, wheeze and weight loss with hypervascular liver lesions: carcinoid syndrome until proven otherwise, likely from metastatic neuroendocrine tumor. Edema and fatigue raise the question of carcinoid heart disease.
Plan:
1. Transthoracic echocardiogram, attention to the right-sided valves.
2. 24-hour urine 5-HIAA (food/med restrictions given) and serum chromogranin A.
3. Referral to medical oncology for tissue diagnosis and management; discussed with her PCP.
Cardiology follow-up depending on echo.

documents.title: Outside lab results received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Results from the cancer center lab (ordered by cardiology): 24-hr urine 5-HIAA 86 mg/24 h (ref 2-9), chromogranin A 412 ng/mL (ref <93). Filed and routed to PCP.

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. LVEF 60% by biplane method. Normal diastolic function for age. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Tricuspid valve leaflets thin and mobile, no regurgitation beyond trace; pulmonic valve normal. Mitral and aortic valves normal. Estimated RVSP normal. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Normal echocardiogram. No evidence of carcinoid valve disease.

documents.title: Cardiology note - echo result
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body: Echo 4/24 normal, EF 60%, right-sided valves normal. No carcinoid heart disease. Urine 5-HIAA markedly elevated at 86. Oncology consult 5/13. Cardiology will see her as needed.

documents.title: Medical Oncology - neuroendocrine consult
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION - NEUROENDOCRINE TUMORS
Date: 05/13/2024
Reason: hypervascular liver lesions with carcinoid syndrome.

63F with prior right breast TNBC (2018) and cervical SCC (2021). Months of flushing, watery diarrhea, nocturnal wheeze and weight loss. CT 4/3: several arterially enhancing liver lesions, largest 2.4 cm. Urine 5-HIAA 86 mg/24 h, chromogranin A 412. Echo 4/24 normal.
Meds: none. NKDA.
Exam: thin, comfortable. Periorbital darkening. No adenopathy. Liver not palpable. Trace ankle edema.

Impression: presentation strongly suggests metastatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor with carcinoid syndrome. Given two prior cancers, tissue is required.
Plan: ultrasound-guided core biopsy of a liver lesion; Ga-68 DOTATATE PET for staging and receptor status. Return with results to start therapy.

conditions.label: Secondary carcinoid tumors of liver
conditions.note: Well-differentiated NET grade 2, Ki-67 4%, midgut origin by CDX2, primary not localized

reports.text: Specimen: liver lesion, ultrasound-guided core biopsy (3 cores). Microscopic: nests and trabeculae of uniform cells with salt-and-pepper chromatin in a vascular stroma. Immunohistochemistry: synaptophysin and chromogranin positive; CDX2 positive; TTF-1 negative; GATA3 negative; p40 negative. Ki-67 proliferation index 4%. Mitoses less than 2 per 2 mm2.
reports.conclusion: Metastatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, grade 2 (Ki-67 4%). Immunoprofile consistent with midgut origin. No features of breast or cervical carcinoma.

documents.title: Ultrasound-guided liver biopsy
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous core biopsy of a liver lesion, 18-gauge, three cores, right intercostal approach. Moderate sedation. No immediate complications; 2-hour observation unremarkable. Discharged home with her sister. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT report
documents.author: nuclear medicine
documents.body:
NUCLEAR MEDICINE - Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT
Date of exam: 05/29/2024
Indication: biopsy-proven metastatic well-differentiated NET, liver; staging.
Findings: the hepatic lesions seen on CT 4/3/2024 show intense somatostatin-receptor uptake (Krenning-equivalent above liver background). No abnormal uptake in the bowel, mesentery, pancreas, lymph nodes, lungs or bones. Physiologic uptake in spleen, adrenals, pituitary and kidneys.
Impression: somatostatin-receptor-avid hepatic metastases. No extrahepatic disease. Primary not localized.

medications.sig: 120 mg deep subcutaneous injection every 28 days, given at the cancer center

documents.title: Medical Oncology follow-up - treatment start
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - NET
Date: 06/10/2024
Results reviewed with patient and sister: liver biopsy shows metastatic well-differentiated NET, grade 2, Ki-67 4%, midgut profile. DOTATATE PET: avid liver metastases only, primary not seen.
Symptoms: flushing 4-5 times a week, 3-4 loose stools daily, night wheeze.
NKDA.
Plan: lanreotide 120 mg deep SC every 28 days, first injection today in the infusion suite; tolerated. Expect GI upset early and some injection-site tenderness. Imaging with multiphase CT every 6 months; 5-HIAA with visits. Liver-directed therapy held in reserve. Copy to PCP and cardiology.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First time I have seen her since the diagnosis. Metastatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor to the liver, grade 2, primary not found, carcinoid syndrome. Echo normal. Lanreotide every 4 weeks at the cancer center since June 10; on her second shot now.
How she is doing: flushing down to once or twice a week, stools 2 a day and more formed. Tolerating the shots. Night wheeze less. Weight holding at 61. Mood: scared at first, steadier now; sister and a friend from school drive her. PHQ-9 6, she does not want counseling referral now but knows it is available.
Rectal bleeding: rare spotting only.
Meds: lanreotide 120 mg q28d (oncology). NKDA.

Exam: vitals charted. Looks better than in March. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Mild bilateral ankle edema, less than before. RUE lymphedema unchanged.

A/P
- Metastatic NET with carcinoid syndrome, responding symptomatically to lanreotide. Oncology leads.
- Radiation proctitis, improved after 2 APC sessions. Anemia improving, CBC today.
- Lymphedema stable.
- Mood: steadier, will keep asking.
Flu/COVID in the fall. RTC 4 months.

events.reason: Enlarging painful purple nodule right chest wall

documents.title: Emergency Department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date: 10/14/2025, arrival 16:20

CC: painful growing purple bump on the right chest.

HPI: 65-year-old woman with prior right breast cancer (lumpectomy, ALND, chemotherapy and radiation, about seven years ago) and cervical cancer (surgery and pelvic radiation 2021), chronic right arm lymphedema, radiation proctitis and carcinoid syndrome from metastatic NET on lanreotide. Two months ago she noticed a small purplish spot on the right chest wall; it has grown quickly and become tender. Came in tonight because it now hurts against her bra and looks darker. Her right arm has been swollen since breast cancer treatment; she wears compression sleeves. No fever, no drainage, no trauma.
Meds: lanreotide 120 mg monthly. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother breast cancer; father MI; sister healthy; no family history of colon cancer, neuroendocrine tumors or sarcomas.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, retired elementary teacher on disability.

Exam: vitals reviewed, afebrile. Right upper chest wall: violaceous nodule roughly 3 cm across, irregular border, fine telangiectatic vessels over it; no discharge, no ulceration. Skin around it thickened. Right arm with non-pitting edema. No palpable axillary lymph nodes. Lungs clear, heart regular.

MDM: rapidly enlarging vascular-appearing lesion in a previously irradiated field with chronic lymphedema. Concern for a vascular malignancy. Discussed with the on-call dermatology service; 4 mm punch biopsy performed at the lesion edge after lidocaine, one suture, hemostasis good. Specimen to pathology.

Disposition: home. Acetaminophen for pain. Wound care given. Pathology to her PCP and the cancer center; urgent oncology follow-up. Return for bleeding, fever or rapid change.

documents.title: I was in the ER
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I wanted you to hear it from me. I went to the ER Tuesday night about the purple bump on my right chest. They did a biopsy. The ER doctor said it might be something from the radiation. I am trying not to panic. Will you get the results?

documents.title: RE: I was in the ER
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me. Yes, the pathology will come to me and to your oncologist. I will call you as soon as I see it, likely in the next day or two. I also booked you with me Monday the 20th so we can sit down together and plan.

conditions.label: Lymphedema-associated angiosarcoma of right chest wall (Stewart-Treves syndrome)

reports.text: Specimen: skin, right chest wall, 4 mm punch biopsy. Clinical: rapidly enlarging violaceous nodule in a previously irradiated field with chronic right arm lymphedema. Microscopic: dermis infiltrated by atypical endothelial cells with enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei forming irregular, anastomosing vascular channels that dissect collagen. Immunostains: CD31 positive, ERG positive in the atypical cells. Cytokeratin negative.
reports.conclusion: Angiosarcoma. Arising in the setting of chronic lymphedema and prior radiation.

documents.title: Biopsy result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Heather with the pathology: angiosarcoma, a cancer of blood vessel cells, in the skin of the right chest wall, the kind that can come up years after radiation and with long-standing lymphedema. Separate from the liver tumor. Told her it needs a sarcoma team quickly and that I have already reached out to the cancer center. She cried, then wanted to know the next steps; we went over Monday's visit. Her sister will come.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - after ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with her sister after Tuesday's ED visit.
Right chest wall nodule over about 2 months, biopsied in the ED; pathology Friday: angiosarcoma (CD31/ERG positive) in the radiated field with her chronic right arm lymphedema. Tender, no bleeding from the biopsy site.
NET: on lanreotide, last CT June stable. Feels otherwise as usual. Weight 61.
Meds: lanreotide 120 mg q28d. NKDA.

Exam: vitals charted. Right upper chest: violaceous nodule ~3 cm, irregular edge, overlying small vessels, biopsy site healing with one suture. Thickened skin around it. No axillary or supraclavicular nodes. RUE non-pitting edema at baseline. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Angiosarcoma, right chest wall, in the setting of lymphedema and prior radiation. Urgent referral to the sarcoma program at the cancer center; I spoke with their intake nurse, consult 10/28. Suture out at day 10, can be done here or there.
2. Metastatic NET, stable, lanreotide continues.
3. Flu (high-dose) and COVID today since she will be in treatment soon.
Spent extended time on counseling; questions answered. I'll stay in touch through this.

documents.title: Sarcoma Oncology consultation
documents.author: sarcoma oncology
documents.body:
SARCOMA MULTIDISCIPLINARY CLINIC - NEW CONSULT
Date: 10/28/2025
Diagnosis: angiosarcoma of the right chest wall skin, biopsy 10/14/2025 (CD31+, ERG+), arising in a previously irradiated field (whole-breast RT 2018) with chronic grade 2 right arm lymphedema after ALND.
Other history: metastatic well-differentiated NET to liver (2024) on lanreotide, stable; cervical SCC 2021, NED; radiation proctitis.
Meds: lanreotide. NKDA.
Exam: right upper chest wall violaceous nodule 3 cm with surrounding skin thickening; no satellite lesions identified on careful inspection; no adenopathy. Right arm lymphedema.

Assessment: localized cutaneous angiosarcoma.
Plan (tumor board): staging CT chest. If localized, wide resection with generous margins and flap reconstruction by surgical oncology and plastics, followed by adjuvant weekly paclitaxel. Re-irradiation not planned given prior dose. Discussed with NET oncology; lanreotide continues.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Indication: staging, angiosarcoma right chest wall. Right anterior chest wall: 3 cm enhancing cutaneous and subcutaneous soft-tissue nodule without involvement of the pectoralis muscle or ribs. Post-treatment change of the right breast. No axillary, internal mammary or mediastinal adenopathy. Lungs clear, no nodules. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Upper abdomen: known hypervascular liver lesions, unchanged from 06/2025.
reports.conclusion: Localized right chest wall lesion. No thoracic metastatic disease.

reports.text: Specimen: right chest wall skin and subcutaneous tissue, wide excision, oriented. Gross: 14 x 11 cm ellipse with a 3.1 cm violaceous nodule. Microscopic: angiosarcoma, as on prior biopsy, confined to dermis and subcutis. Margins: all margins negative, closest 1.4 cm (superior).

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Surgical Oncology
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/19/2025, discharged 11/21/2025
Diagnosis: angiosarcoma of the right chest wall (radiation and lymphedema associated).
Procedure 11/19: wide resection of right chest wall skin and subcutaneous tissue with local flap reconstruction (surgical oncology with plastic surgery). EBL minimal. Drain placed.
Course: uncomplicated. Pain controlled with oral agents. Flap viable throughout. Tolerating diet, ambulating, voiding. Drain output decreasing; goes home with drain and teaching.
Other active issues: metastatic NET to liver on lanreotide (next dose due 12/4 at the cancer center); radiation proctitis, no bleeding this admission; RUE lymphedema, no BP or sticks right arm.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: oxycodone/acetaminophen 5/325 one tab every 6 h as needed, 20 tablets; lanreotide 120 mg every 28 days (unchanged).
Follow-up: surgical oncology 12/2 for drain and pathology; sarcoma oncology 12/17 to start adjuvant chemotherapy. Final pathology pending at discharge.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call. Home with sister staying. Pain 3/10, using 1-2 oxycodone/APAP a day, tapering. Drain 20-30 mL/day, serous. No fever, flap looks pink per pt. BMs ok with prune juice. Has surgical f/u 12/2. Reviewed when to call. PCP aware.

12/02/2025, two weeks after wide resection of right chest wall angiosarcoma with local flap.
Drain removed today. Incision and flap healing well, no seroma, no infection.
Final pathology reviewed: angiosarcoma 3.1 cm, all margins negative, closest 1.4 cm.
Off oxycodone, acetaminophen only. NKDA.
Plan: proceed to adjuvant chemotherapy with sarcoma oncology 12/17. Surgical follow-up in 3 months.

12/17/2025

Plan as discussed: adjuvant paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 IV weekly for 12 doses, cycle 1 day 1 today. Premedication per protocol. Labs before each dose. Lanreotide continues on its schedule.

03/04/2026: dose 12 of 12 of weekly paclitaxel given today. Adjuvant therapy complete.
Tolerated with fatigue and thinning hair.

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two days after her last paclitaxel. Wide resection of the right chest wall angiosarcoma in November, margins clear, then 12 weekly doses, done Wednesday.
Tired, napping afternoons, but eating. Hair thin, wearing a scarf. NET symptoms quiet on lanreotide; stools formed. Proctitis: no bleeding this winter. Weight 59.5.
Meds: lanreotide 120 mg q28d. Paclitaxel finished. NKDA.

Exam: vitals charted. Tired but bright. Right chest flap healed, no new nodules on chest wall or right arm. RUE lymphedema at baseline. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft.

A/P
- Angiosarcoma right chest wall s/p resection and adjuvant paclitaxel. Surveillance per sarcoma team, CT in May. She knows to show me or them any new purple spot on the chest or arm.
- Metastatic NET, stable on lanreotide.
- Anemia after chemo, CBC today.
- Mammogram on hold until sarcoma team clears. DXA deferred again.
RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.
